cleanIntro: The 555 is the light alloy-receiver half of a pair — Savage builds the same over/under as the steel-receivered Model 550 and the alloy-receivered Model 555 — and the teardown is the classic break-gun split: forend off, action open, barrels off the frame. Two things vary from gun to gun and neither is on the model number: whether yours has extractors or ejectors, and which chokes are in the barrels. Both change how the gun behaves in your hands, and one of them bounds what ammunition you may fire.

steps.title: Model 550 or Model 555 — read the receiver, not the box
steps.action: Savage builds this over/under in two configurations and they are not the same gun: the Model 550 has a steel receiver, the Model 555 an alloy one. That is a weight and a wear difference, not a badge — an alloy receiver is lighter to carry and less tolerant of being levered on during assembly. Everything below is written for the 555, and the manual covers both, so check which one you are holding before you take anything apart.
steps.prose: Nothing else in the teardown branches on it; the receiver material is what the model number means here.
steps.quote: Your Stevens shotgun is offered in two configurations: Model 550 (steel receiver) and Model 555 (light weight alloy receiver).
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Introduction, p.3

steps.title: Safety fully rearward — the ‘S’ shows, the red dot is covered
steps.action: The safety on a 550 or 555 is the rectangular slider on the rear tang, directly behind the top lever. Push it fully rearward until the engraved ‘S’ is exposed and the red dot is hidden. It is a manual safety, not an automatic one — opening and closing the breech does NOT put it back on, which is the habit that catches people coming off other break guns. Never leave it parked between positions; if it is not all the way forward or all the way back you cannot tell which state it is in.
steps.prose: This is the same control that selects which barrel fires, so get used to finding it by feel.
steps.quote: On the Stevens Model 550 and Model 555, the safety is a rectangular button which slides forward and backward on the rear tang directly behind the top lever of the shotgun.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 2, Two Position Manual Safety, p.7
steps.warn: THE SAFETY ON YOUR SHOTGUN IS MANUAL AND NOT AUTOMATIC.

steps.title: Top lever right, barrels down — and keep your face out of line
steps.action: Push the top lever fully to the right with your thumb; it should move easily, so do not force it. Pull down on the barrels until the action is fully open and the chambers are exposed. Keep your face out of line with the chambers as they open, because on an ejector gun the cases leave under spring force and they leave rearward.
steps.prose: When the action is open and empty is the only condition in which this gun cannot fire.
steps.quote: 2. Move the TOP LEVER to the right as far as it will go (see FIGURE 3) to open the action. Do not use excessive force, the lever should move easily.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Unloading, p.10
steps.warn: NEVER PUT YOUR FACE IN CLOSE PROXIMITY (OR IN LINE) WITH THE CHAMBERS WHEN OPENING THE ACTION.

steps.title: Extractors or ejectors — know which 555 you have
steps.action: Savage fits some of these guns with extractors and others with ejectors, and the difference shows up the instant you open the action. With extractors the shells lift back far enough to pinch out with your fingers and stay put. With ejectors the fired cases are thrown clear under spring force while unfired shells only rise enough to grasp. Open the action once with snap caps and watch which happens, because an ejector gun will fling a case past your ear if you open it casually.
steps.prose: Nothing on the outside of the gun tells you, and the model number does not either.
steps.caution: ALWAYS BE SURE TO WEAR ADEQUATE EYE AND EAR PROTECTION
steps.quote: Certain Stevens shotguns are fitted with extractors and other with ejectors.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Extractors Or Ejectors, p.10

steps.title: Steel shot — Modified is the tightest choke you may use
steps.action: If you shoot steel, read the notches on the choke before loading. Steel shot is much harder than lead and rides in a plastic wad to spare the bore, but forced through anything tighter than Modified it damages the barrel and can injure you or a bystander. Full, Improved Modified, or any choke of greater constriction than Modified is out with steel — and Savage voids the warranty over it, which tells you how seriously they mean it.
steps.prose: The identification notches on the choke's end are how you read constriction in poor light.
steps.quote: THE USE OF A FULL CHOKE (I), IMPROVED MODIFIED CHOKE (II), OR ANY OTHER CHOKE WITH A GREATER CONSTRICTION THAN MODIFIED (III) WILL ALSO VOID THE WARRANTY.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Loading, p.8
steps.warn: Steel shot ceiling on the Model 555: MODIFIED. Nothing tighter.

steps.title: Release button first, then the release lever
steps.action: Close the action, then find the release lever on the underside of the forend. It is a two-stage catch and the order matters: press the RELEASE BUTTON first, and only then pull the release lever. Trying to lever it without the button will not release it and will bend something. Once the lever is pulled, the forend comes away from the barrels.
steps.prose: Confirm the chambers are empty before you close the action for this step.
steps.quote: 4. Press the RELEASE BUTTON (see FIGURE 8) first and then pull the RELEASE LEVER.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Removing The Barrel Assembly, p.11

steps.title: Forend off — now the barrels are free to leave the frame
steps.action: Pull the forend away from the barrels and set it down. Understand what you have just changed: the forend is what retains the barrels on the hinge, so from this moment opening the action lets the barrel assembly come off the frame entirely. Keep a hand under the barrels from here on, or a two-pound set of tubes hits the bench muzzle-first.
steps.prose: This is the step where dropped barrels happen on break guns.
steps.quote: BE CAREFUL – WHEN THE FOREND HAS BEEN REMOVED, OPENING THE ACTION WILL CAUSE THE BARRELS TO SEPARATE FROM THE FRAME.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Removing The Barrel Assembly, p.11
steps.warn: With the forend off, opening the action releases the barrels.

steps.title: Top lever right, lift the barrels off the hinge
steps.action: With a hand supporting the barrels, move the top lever right and open the action. The barrel assembly lifts straight off the hinge pin — no force, no twisting. You are now down to three pieces: barrels, forend, and the stock-and-frame unit with the locks in it.
steps.prose: Lay the barrels down on their side rather than standing them in a corner.
steps.quote: 7. The barrel assembly will now separate from the frame.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Removing The Barrel Assembly, p.11

steps.title: Both bores from the chamber end, out the muzzle
steps.action: Lay the barrels horizontally with the muzzles pointing away from you. Always start the rod at the chamber end and push through and out the muzzle — reversing that drags fouling back over the chamber and can damage the crown, which is the last thing the shot column touches. Solvent on the brush, several passes, then swap the brush for a patch tip and push clean patches through until they run clean, then one oiled patch, then one dry patch to take the excess back off.
steps.prose: Do both barrels; on an over/under it is easy to do the bottom one twice and the top one never.
steps.caution: CHECK THE BORES CAREFULLY WHEN DONE TO BE SURE THERE ARE NO OBSTRUCTIONS (I.E. PIECES OF CLEANING PATCH, ETC.).
steps.quote: ALWAYS STARTING FROM THE CHAMBER END, PUSH THE CLEANING ROD THROUGH THE BORE AND OUT THE MUZZLE END.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 5, Cleaning And Care, p.13

steps.title: Chokes out, threads greased, and never fire without them
steps.action: Unload and open the action before you touch a choke. Back each choke out with the supplied wrench, wipe the threads and the seat in the barrel, and put a thin coat of light gun grease or choke-tube lubricant on the threads before they go back. Screw them in firmly without over-tightening. A barrel fired with no choke installed has the bore damaged where the thread run is — that is the whole reason the tubes must go back before the gun does.
steps.prose: The 12, 20, 28 and .410 guns ship with five interchangeable Beretta/Benelli-style chokes and a wrench.
steps.caution: NEVER USE A CHOKE THAT IS BENT OR OUT-OF-ROUND.
steps.quote: FIRING A SHOTGUN WITHOUT A CHOKE INSTALLED MAY RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE BORE AND POSSIBLE INJURY TO YOU OR A BYSTANDER.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 4, Screw-In Choke System, p.12

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Three pieces on the bench: the barrel assembly, the forend, and the stock-and-frame. That is the whole of the Model 555 teardown Savage publishes — the locks, the top lever, the ejector or extractor mechanism and the trigger all stay in the frame. Savage states outright that further disassembly is a gunsmith's job or its own service department's, so there is no deeper branch to walk here.
steps.prose: With the forend off, take the chance to inspect the underside of the barrels — it is the only time you see it.
steps.quote: NOTE: Further disassembly of your shotgun is not recommended and should be done only by a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms Service Department.
steps.cite: STEVENS BY Savage Arms — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — STEVENS Model 550 and Model 555 — UNKNOWN — no part number, revision code or date code is printed anywhere in this document — Section 3, Reassembling The Barrel And Forend, p.11

deepAbsentReason: Savage publishes no deeper teardown for the Model 555 and declines to recommend one: "NOTE: Further disassembly of your shotgun is not recommended and should be done only by a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms Service Department." (Section 3, Reassembling The Barrel And Forend, p.11). The barrels-off state walked above is the maximum owner disassembly. The frame still holds the locks, hammers, top lever, trigger and the extractor or ejector mechanism, and Savage's Section 5 maintenance is explicitly an INSPECTION regime for those — look at the firing pin holes, the extractors or ejectors and the frame surfaces with the action open — not a teardown. Authoring a lock or ejector strip for this gun would be publishing a procedure the maker withholds.

cleaning.name: BORES — BOTH BARRELS
tasks: Lay the barrels horizontally, muzzles away from you, action open
ALWAYS start the rod at the chamber end and push out the muzzle
Solvent on the brush, several passes per barrel
Swap to a patch tip and push clean patches through until they run clean
One oil-saturated patch, then one dry patch to take off the excess
Check both bores for patch fragments before putting the gun away

cleaning.name: CHOKES
tasks: Unload and open the action before changing or verifying a choke
Thin coat of light gun grease or choke-tube lubricant on the threads before fitting
Firmly screwed in, but do not over-tighten
Never use a bent or out-of-round choke
STEEL SHOT: nothing tighter than Modified (III) — Full (I) and Improved Modified (II) are out

cleaning.name: FRAME & METAL SURFACES
tasks: Open the action first so all surfaces are reachable
Soft cloth to lift off mud, twigs and grass
Thin coat of gun oil on all cleaned metal; rub to lift any rust
Clean and lightly oil interior metal surfaces where you can reach them
A VERY THIN FILM OF OIL IS SUFFICIENT — DO NOT OVER OIL

cleaning.name: INSPECTION — WITH THE FOREND OFF
tasks: Look down both barrels from the BREECH end for obstructions, nicks, rust or pitting
Run your fingers down the outside of the barrels feeling for bulges
Inspect the frame around the firing pin holes, and the extractors or ejectors, for wear
Inspect the sides and underside of the barrels — visible only with the forend removed
Examine the stock and forend for cracks or splits
Re-verify the two-position safety works before the gun is loaded again

reassembly: Realign the barrel assembly with the frame and close the action carefully — no force.
Place the rear of the forend against the frame, then rotate it upward toward the barrels; it should move easily into place.
Press the RELEASE BUTTON first, then push the RELEASE LEVER until it locks.
Open and close the action to verify the barrels and forend are correctly assembled — it should close easily with an audible click.
Confirm the top lever returns to its rearward position; if it does not, the action is NOT locked and the gun must not be fired.
Re-verify the two-position safety as described in Section 2 before the gun is loaded.
fncheck: With the gun assembled and the chambers confirmed empty, close the action and check the top lever has returned to pointing rearward — if it has not, the action is not fully locked and the gun does not get fired. Slide the safety fully rearward and forward and confirm the ‘S’ and the red dot appear as they should, then check the barrel selector reveals ‘U’ to the right and ‘O’ to the left. Open the action once more and look through both bores from the breech end for any patch left behind. Anything that feels or sounds different from usual is a stop-and-see-a-gunsmith, not a shoot-and-see.
